title: Qualcomm To Reportedly Conduct Global Layoffs In Performance-Driven Overhaul
gist: A SemiWiki forum post relaying a Firstpost/Reuters report says Qualcomm will notify employees of performance-focused job cuts starting in November, with the number undisclosed. Context given: about 52,000 employees as of September 2025, Apple revenue declining faster than expected, and a plan for non-handset businesses to make up most chip sales by fiscal 2027, while the stock is up about 1.5% in 2026 against a 60% rise in the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index.

insights.claim: Qualcomm will begin notifying employees of job cuts in November after annual performance reviews, per a CEO memo reviewed by Reuters; the number affected was not disclosed.
insights.speaker: Barnsley
insights.so_what: Layoff scale is still unknown; watch for disclosure in filings.
insights.locator: Qualcomm plans to cut jobs worldwide

insights.claim: Cristiano Amon said the move is intended to build a stronger performance culture and address employees who consistently failed to meet expectations.
insights.speaker: Barnsley
insights.so_what: Management is framing cuts as performance-driven rather than a revenue emergency.
insights.locator: Amon said the move was intended

insights.claim: Amon wrote that 'As we have expanded the business, so have the competencies and skills we require', adding Qualcomm must ensure the right people are in the right roles.
insights.speaker: Cristiano Amon
insights.so_what: Signals a skills mix shift toward new businesses such as data centres.
insights.quote: As we have expanded the business, so have the competencies and skills we require

insights.claim: Qualcomm had approximately 52,000 employees globally as of September 2025, most of them full-time.
insights.speaker: Barnsley
insights.so_what: Base for sizing any percentage cut once it is disclosed.

insights.claim: Rising memory prices are weighing on consumer electronics demand in key markets, hurting Qualcomm's core smartphone chip business.
insights.speaker: Barnsley
insights.so_what: Memory cost inflation is a drag on handset unit demand and thus on Qualcomm.
insights.locator: The job cuts come as Qualcomm faces challenges

insights.claim: In late July Qualcomm forecast quarterly profit below market expectations and warned revenue from Apple products would decline faster than previously anticipated.
insights.speaker: Barnsley
insights.so_what: Apple modem revenue roll-off is the largest known revenue headwind.
insights.locator: In its latest earnings report in late July

insights.claim: Qualcomm expects growth in data centres and other non-handset businesses to more than offset the Apple-related revenue decline by fiscal 2027, and expects most chip sales to come from outside smartphones in fiscal 2027.
insights.speaker: Barnsley
insights.so_what: Core diversification claim to hold management to in FY27 reporting.
insights.locator: However, the company expects growth in data centres

insights.claim: Qualcomm is seeking to diversify by expanding into the fast-growing AI data centre market and other businesses.
insights.speaker: Barnsley
insights.so_what: Re-rating depends on data centre traction.
insights.locator: Qualcomm is seeking to diversify beyond smartphones

insights.claim: Qualcomm shares have gained around 1.5% in 2026 versus more than 12% for the S&P 500 and nearly 60% for the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index.
insights.speaker: Barnsley
insights.so_what: Large relative underperformance reflects market skepticism of the non-handset pivot.
insights.locator: Qualcomm's shares have gained around 1.5 per cent
